turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Temp's 98.6, heart rate 118, respirations 22, oxygen sat 99 percent. He fussed in the waiting room, then settled.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks. It's been a rough few nights.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come on in. I'm Dr. Shah. What's been going on?
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, his ear. He had a cold, and now he's crying at night and grabbing at it.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Owen, where does it hurt?
[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): Ear.
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The right one. He's four, and he clams up when he feels lousy.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it hurt right this minute?
[SEG0009] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mom, when did the ear pain start?
[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two nights— well, actually, the cold came first and then...
[SEG0012] person_4 (PATIENT): Mommy.
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, bud. Three nights. Tuesday night was the first time he woke up screaming, so three nights, not two.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): During the cold, cough, runny nose?
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Runny nose, yeah, and a little cough. Cough's mostly gone. The nose is still sort of...
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still running today?
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I wipe and then it's dry.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever you measured?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I checked a few times. No fever.
[SEG0020] person_4 (PATIENT): Hot.
[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What he means— Grandma had him yesterday and said he was hot, burning up. I took his temp when I got him and it was normal. So I don't think he had a fever.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Grandma felt he was hot, your thermometer was normal, and he said hot. No documented fever, then. I'm leaving that unsettled.
[SEG0023] person_1 (NURSE): He didn't feel warm to me either, and the 98.6 was just before we walked in.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the crying only at night?
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Around midnight, yeah, he wails. Days are better. He won't lie on that right side.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is he pulling at the ear?
[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Constantly. The right ear. Tugs it and whines.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Diarrhea?
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No diarrhea. And no rash on his skin today.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Drainage from the ear, or trouble hearing you?
[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hearing, I really can't tell. Drainage... mm, sometimes, not really. Maybe one speck of crust. I might have imagined that.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): How's drinking and eating?
[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Drinking fine, milk and water. Eating less than his usual.
[SEG0036] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): You don't want to eat?
[SEG0038] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's talking about the crackers. Appetite's down, not gone. He'll still do yogurt most days.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): What pain medicine has he had?
[SEG0040] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Children's Tylenol, by mouth. A hundred and sixty milligrams, every six hours or so when he's hurting.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you hit every dose?
[SEG0042] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I think so, except I might've skipped the middle-of-the-night one last night. I'm not sure.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you try ibuprofen?
[SEG0044] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0045] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He didn't like the taste, but he did get it the first day. Five milliliters, a hundred milligrams, by mouth. Then I stopped it.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did you stop it, and why?
[SEG0047] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yesterday morning. His stomach got crampy after, so only Tylenol since then.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any drops or cold syrup at home?
[SEG0049] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Bought children's Dimetapp, never gave it. Ofloxacin ear drops were prescribed last year and I never filled them. He never took either one.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Those stay off the list, then. Medicine allergies?
[SEG0051] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um. Amoxicillin, long ago. He got a rash, maybe. I was never sure it was actually the amoxicillin.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Timing, what the rash looked like, the dose?
[SEG0053] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I can't date it. He was a toddler. Pink spots, I think, not hives. We stopped it the day I saw the spots. Dose, I shouldn't guess.
[SEG0054] person_4 (PATIENT): Rash.
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): Owen, rash?
[SEG0056] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0057] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He doesn't remember any of that. I'm still on the fence about it. No other allergies, and no food allergies.
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has he had an ear infection before?
[SEG0059] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One last winter. It cleared. No surgeries, and no ear tubes.
[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family history of ear trouble?
[SEG0061] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His dad had tubes when he was little. I didn't.
[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is he in daycare? I got distracted, sorry—
[SEG0063] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0064] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wait, you asked daycare. He says no because he wanted to stay home today. He goes four days a week. We live with my mom and she keeps him the other days.
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anyone smoke at home?
[SEG0066] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nobody smokes.
[SEG0067] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. I'm going to look in the ears with a light, Owen.
[SEG0068] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0069] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You can look. The no doesn't mean no with him.
[SEG0070] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right eardrum is a little pink. Not bulging, landmarks are still there. Left ear is clear.
[SEG0071] person_3 (DOCTOR): Throat's mildly red, no pus. Neck is soft, no big lymph nodes. Lungs sound clear. Belly's soft, no rash on the skin today, and he doesn't look toxic on your lap.
[SEG0072] person_4 (PATIENT): Hurt.
[SEG0073] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Does that mean the ear's infected?

[SEG0074] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me think it through. It might be a very early ear infection, or it might just be congestion left over from the cold. The drum isn't bulging, so I won't call it a definite bacterial otitis.
[SEG0075] person_3 (DOCTOR): Watchful waiting today, no antibiotic to start now. Keep Tylenol, one hundred sixty milligrams by mouth every six hours if the pain needs it. Leave the ibuprofen off.
[SEG0076] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What if he screams again tonight?

[SEG0077] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the ear pain and night crying aren't better in two days, or you measure a fever of 100.4 or more, start the backup. I'll send cefdinir, seven milliliters of the 250 per 5 milliliter suspension, by mouth, once a day, for five days. We're avoiding amoxicillin because of that possible rash.
[SEG0078] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So I don't start it unless one of those happens?

[SEG0079] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Hold it unless then. If he's not better in two days, come back and see me too. Stiff neck, stops drinking, or you can't wake him, skip the wait and go to the ER. Nurse will print the only-if instructions at the desk.

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Transcript mentions amoxicillin only as a possible allergy, not as a medication status discontinued.

omissions.text: Associated cold symptoms were reported: runny nose and a little cough; the cough is mostly gone and the runny nose is intermittent/possibly still present.
No measured fever was reported by the family member despite checking multiple times.

Drainage from the ear and hearing trouble were specifically asked about; hearing trouble was uncertain ('can't tell') and ear drainage was not really present/uncertain aside from maybe one speck of crust.
Drinking was reported as fine, specifically milk and water.
Ibuprofen details were incomplete: 5 mL (100 mg) by mouth was given only on the first day, then stopped yesterday morning because it seemed to make his stomach crampy.
Children's Dimetapp was bought but never given, and ofloxacin ear drops from last year were prescribed but never filled/taken.
No other medication allergies were reported, and no food allergies.
Past history included one prior ear infection last winter that cleared.
Daycare history was initially contradicted by the child but clarified by the family member: he does attend daycare four days a week, and maternal grandmother watches him on the other days.
